correctness.independent_verification: Independently evaluated all five prime-tail finite product inequalities using fractions (p=11,13,17,19,23), all four exact separation inequalities, exact rational inequality 125/91>1+29^{-3}, constructed 16 rational c_S and conditional masses, and proved sum exactly 1 by algebra. Finite checks are not used as a substitute for Nagura theorem or the infinite greedy subsum/density proof. Source check.py and RESULT.md inspected.
correctness.rationale: On squarefree n, F(n)=σ_{−3}(n)=∏_{p|n}(1+p^{−3}). Log-weights for p≥11 satisfy every dominance-reversal tail covering inequality: five rationally checked small tail prime cases p=11,13,17,19,23, and Nagura’s unconditional prime in every (x,6x/5), x≥25, gives all p≥29 via ≥(125/91)y/(1+y)>y≥log(1+y), y=p^{−3}. Summable subsum greedy lemma fills exactly [1,T] after exponentiating finite-subsum closure. The four small weights p=2,3,5,7 strictly dominate *all* following weights by exact rational bounds, separating exactly 16 c_S[1,T] bands. CRT valuation restrictions modulo p² plus the convergent squarefree sieve give density (6/π²)∏_{p∈S}1/(p+1)∏_{p∈B\S}p/(p+1), with all 16 conditional weights summing to 1. Density is of inputs, not distribution of values within intervals.
